newsitem.title: USA: South Carolina drownings probe yields little.
newsitem.headline: South Carolina drownings probe yields little.

text.p: The driver of a car that plunged into a lake killing all five passengers had no medical condition that would have prevented him from controlling the vehicle, according to autopsy results released on Tuesday.

Seven people including five members of one family drowned Saturday in John D. Long Lake, where Susan Smith drowned her two young sons in 1994. A car with four children and an adult rolled into the lake and two adults died trying to save them.

Union County Sheriff Howard Wells on Tuesday said autopsies confirmed the victims had drowned but shed no light on why the car rolled down a steep ramp and into the lake. It was the same ramp Smith used to roll her car into the lake on Oct. 25, 1994, with her sons Michael and Alex strapped inside.
Smith set off a nationwide search when she said a black man had stolen her car and kidnapped the children. She admitted nine days later that she had drowned her sons.

Angie and Tim Phillips and some friends went to the lake Saturday to look at memorials honouring the Smith boys. Angie Phillips, 22, and four others left the car while her husband stayed inside with their three daughters and another child. Officials said the lights were on and the engine was running.
The vehicle moved between two markers, over a small tree and down the hill into the lake. Angie Phillips and Sidney White drowned trying to save the others.
White's common-law wife Sonya and one of her daughters ran for help while another daughter remained at the scene.

The car was found upside down in 20 feet of water with the gearshift in the park position. Wells said investigators do not know why it went forward but the absence of marks on the ground showed there had been no attempt to brake or steer it.

"I'm not going to rule anything out," Wells said. He said alcohol was consumed at the Phillips home before the group went to the lake and he has asked the state Law Enforcement Division to complete toxicology tests on Tim Phillips.
He also said beer cans were found in the vehicle.
Officials identified the dead as Tim Phillips, 26, his wife, Angela, their children, Courtney, 4, Meleana, 1, and Kinsleigh, 4 months, Cody Roodvoets, 3, and Sidney White, 29.
